Its a solid little gravity-based physics puzzler. Deaths can be infuriating though. You accidently hit a wrong button and you will most likely have to start the level over.

+ If you like Precision Platformers, or "I wanna be the guy" games, then you will like this.

- If you dislike hard platformers, no-frills or old school games, then don't bother with this.

Gravity Den is a puzzle-platformer that builds its entire identity around the clever use of gravity as a gameplay mechanic. Developed by DiPi and published by Volens Nolens Games, the game follows the story of Den, a small one-eyed alien whose spaceship has crash-landed on a mysterious planet. To find his way home, he must traverse a series of tricky levels where traditional platforming rules are turned upside down—literally. The ability to manipulate gravity allows him to walk on ceilings, run along walls, and shift orientation to tackle environments that would otherwise be impossible to navigate. This mechanic is at the heart of the experience, giving the game its charm and its challenge.

The game features three large worlds, each containing fifty levels, gradually ramping up in complexity as new obstacles, traps, and hazards are introduced. Early stages allow players to experiment with the basics of gravity manipulation in relatively safe environments, but as the adventure continues, the difficulty rises dramatically. Levels begin to demand precise timing, quick reflexes, and near-perfect execution of gravity shifts in order to succeed. In addition to simply reaching the exit, many levels also encourage players to collect stars, which unlock additional content and create a strong incentive for replayability. These stars add a layer of challenge beyond just finishing a stage, requiring mastery rather than mere survival.

Visually, Gravity Den embraces a retro pixel-art style that complements its straightforward mechanics. The graphics are not elaborate, but they suit the minimalist design philosophy of the game, focusing more on clarity and function than spectacle. The alien protagonist has a quirky, endearing look, and the colorful environments manage to feel distinct despite the limited style. The soundtrack and sound effects provide a light, arcade-like atmosphere, though they can become repetitive over time, especially when a difficult stage requires multiple retries. The simplicity of the presentation works in the game’s favor, even if it lacks the polish or detail found in more modern platformers.

What defines the experience most is its difficulty. Gravity Den does not shy away from challenging the player, often demanding precision that borders on unforgiving. Small mistakes usually result in instant failure, requiring the player to start over. For some, this creates an addictive loop of trial and error, where each attempt feels like a step closer to mastery. For others, the steep learning curve may feel punishing rather than rewarding. The control scheme itself is functional but not as tight as one might expect for a game that demands pinpoint accuracy. Den’s movements can feel overly sensitive, and the ninety-degree turns required for wall and ceiling walking sometimes lack the smoothness needed in tense situations. These issues are not game-breaking, but they do contribute to frustration in more demanding levels.

The game’s structure encourages players to revisit levels and aim for perfection. Unlocking additional content through star collection, chasing faster times, and attempting hardcore bonus stages add significant replay value. However, the repetitiveness of the core loop—entering a level, failing repeatedly until execution is perfect, then moving on—means that not everyone will find long-term satisfaction. Still, for fans of challenging platformers, the sheer volume of content across three worlds and over one hundred and fifty levels is impressive, especially given the game’s modest price point.

Gravity Den ultimately succeeds in delivering a tough but rewarding puzzle-platforming experience that leans heavily on its central mechanic. It offers plenty of content, a charmingly retro presentation, and a design philosophy that will resonate with players who enjoy precision-based challenges. On the other hand, its steep difficulty spikes, occasionally imprecise controls, and repetitive structure will likely deter more casual players. It is not a game built for everyone, but for those who thrive on mastering difficult levels and enjoy experimenting with gravity-based puzzles, Gravity Den is an inventive and affordable option worth exploring.

Купил эту игру, думал, будет легко — наивный! Оказалось, что гравитация тут не просто фишка, а настоящий тиран, который только и ждёт момента, чтобы отправить тебя в вечный полёт за пределы экрана.

Теперь я понимаю, почему мой кот смотрит на меня с таким снисходительным выражением лица — он тоже знает, что такое неудачные попытки.

Графика приятная, музыка умиротворяющая (пока не начнёшь злиться), но управление… Управление — это отдельная история. То персонаж летит как ракета, то тормозит как старый троллейбус. Инерция? Не, не слышали! Тут всё по принципу «захотел полететь — лети, пока не упрёшься в невидимую стену».

В общем, если вы любите игры, где нужно:
[list]
    [*]Много раз умирать
    [*]Ненавидеть края экрана
    [*]Учиться летать (и не только в игре)
    [*]Коллекционировать звёзды (как хобби)
[/list]

То Gravity Den — это ваш выбор!

[h1]Gravity Den: Обзор[/h1]

[i]Приготовьтесь управлять гравитацией в Gravity Den, уникальном платформере с харизматичным инопланетным героем.[/i]

Введение:

Ден, одноглазый инопланетянин, потерпел крушение на планете, где каждый может управлять гравитацией. Воспользуйтесь этим необычным даром, чтобы помочь Дену найти его потерянный корабль.

Геймплей:

Gravity Den предлагает захватывающий геймплей, где вы управляете гравитацией вокруг Дена. Вы сможете ходить по стенам, летать в воздухе и преодолевать различные препятствия, изменяя направление притяжения.

Каждый уровень предлагает уникальные испытания и ловушки. Собирайте звезды, чтобы открывать новые комнаты с более сложными препятствиями. Соревнуйтесь с друзьями и улучшайте свои результаты, проходя уровни на время.

Уровни:

Игра включает в себя три огромные локации по 50 уровней в каждой. Каждая локация отличается своим дизайном, ловушками и препятствиями, которые будут проверять ваши навыки и сообразительность.

Графика и производительность:

Gravity Den отличается яркой и выразительной графикой, которая создает захватывающий научно-фантастический мир. Игра оптимизирована для работы на компьютерах со средними характеристиками, обеспечивая плавный и приятный игровой процесс.

Вердикт:

Gravity Den - это уникальный и захватывающий платформер, который предлагает свежий взгляд на управление персонажем. Благодаря интуитивному управлению, разнообразным уровням и соревновательному элементу Gravity Den придется по вкусу любителям головоломок и платформеров всех возрастов.

I've read from other comments about how bad the controls are, but still decided to try it out because it is on %90 sale.

My 2 main issues with the controls are; 
When you are dropping you gain a sideways momentum for NO REASON AT ALL... So even when trying to make a small few pixel move throws you farther away when it shouldn't. Same happens when you make a gravity shift on the air. Not only that, when you change gravity to opposite directions, you go on for about 5 more block to your previous direction before you actually start moving the opposite way, this is f*kng ridiculous!

And second most annoying thing is, if you ever played mario or any other platformer games you know that you'd have some leeway when you move out of the screen, if you turn back before you're gone too far you're still alive on those. For this game you are dead when you just get the edge of the screen even if you were still visible on the screen, controls doesn't even let you come back to recover, you just fall out and die.

Overall, get it on cheap if you want to kill an hour or two but don't expect any masterpiece here. It's just a subpar platformer.

Oyunda, bir gezegene düşen ve yere çakılan Den adında tek gözlü bir uzaylı yer almaktadır. Oyun, Den'in kayıp uzay gemisine ulaşmasına yardımcı olmak için yerçekimini kontrol etme konseptine dayanmaktadır.

Oyun, Den'in etrafındaki yerçekimini kontrol ederek duvarlardan geçmesine, havada uçmasına ve hatta tavanda yürümesine izin veriyor. Üç devasa konum ve her konumda 50 seviye ile oyun, oyuncuların oyunda ilerlemek için üstesinden gelmesi gereken çeşitli tuzaklar ve engeller sunar.

Oyun başarımlara sahiptir ve oyuncuları karmaşık engellere sahip yeni odaların kilidini açmak için her seviyede yıldız toplamaya teşvik eder. Oyuncular ayrıca seviyeleri olabildiğince hızlı tamamlayarak sıralamalarını yükseltebilirler.

Genel olarak Gravity Den, benzersiz bir oyun mekaniği sunan eğlenceli ve zorlu bir bulmaca-platform oyunudur. Oyunun basit ama etkili grafikleri ve müzikleri genel deneyime katkıda bulunuyor. Eğer bulmaca-platform oyunlarından hoşlanıyorsanız, Gravity Den kesinlikle göz atmaya değer.

Jogo bem simples mas legal de jogar, tu morre bem rápido se não tiver habilidade e bons reflexos. 

Gravity Den 6/10

I loved this game, and can't believe it has so few reviews! It's a polished platformer with precision controls, consistent physics, beautiful pixel art, a fun sound track, and plenty of puzzle-rific levels!
If you love puzzle platformers, this one delivers in spades!

I have only 2 small complaints, and they are both about the controller (since I felt the game was WAY better using a Steam Controller or Xbox controller):
1) You do have to configure the controller (and if you use the analog stick for movement there is a glitch where I kept entering door #1 rather than it letting me walk past it, but the D-Pad had no such problem)
2) The on-screen directions only show WASD + Arrows (it'd be nice to have alternate sprites for D-Pad directions + XYAB)

I guess there is 1 *tiny* critique, which is just that the art definitely looks kid friendly, but the puzzles are pretty brutal. I'm not saying they need to change the art, but something like Super Meat Boy advertises its difficulty in part through it's art style.  So maybe just the steam banner and thumbnail should be a more grueling scene of complex platforming.

That's it! And those are pretty dang small critiques, which shows just how polished and perfect this cute platformer was.

This is a more fully developed VVVVVV x4....You can switch gravity in 4 directions, moving your one eyed avatar, avoiding dangers, collecting keys and stars!

If you like VVVVVV you will most likely love this one.  If you didn't like VVVVVV, you still might like this one, because you are less constrained in your controls.  There is much more depth to its art design as well.

The Pixelated art design is great!  It is a very colorful, up beat approach to the dungeon aesthetic and the the music is quick tempo, helping to drive you towards your goal.

ACHIEVEMENTS:  No time trials here (which makes me very happy) and achievements are dished out mainly based on regular playthrough.

Amo los juegos de plataformas, y este pese al buen diseño que tiene el juego me es imposible recomendarlo,  a continuación explicaré por qué:

* La mayoría de las veces no morirás por pinchos o enemigos, morirás por la misma pantalla, si el personaje por un mínimo cálculo erroneo toca un borde, simplemente desaparecerá aún hayas hecho las cosas bien.

* El control es muy difícil e inexacto y a  veces no responde a tiempo (NO PIENSES JUGARLO EN TECLADO, ES IMPOSIBLE)

* El movimiento del personaje es muy rápido, y esto no está mal en otro tipo de juegos, pero no en este que demanda precisión al 100%, ni un milímetro más, ni uno menos. 

* Las primeras dos zonas son pasables, la tercera es exageradamente complicada, y la cuarta zona entra en terreno de lo impasable, esto es típico de los juegos contemporáneos en dónde la palabra HARDCORE se la toman muy a pecho y en vez de ser un juego difícil resulta frustrante.

*Encima de que el juego es mounstruosamente difícil, ¡te cuentan el tiempo!, sólo faltaría un límite de vidas para volverlo totalmente miserable.

*No hay jefes, zonas de bonus, power-ups, ni nada que no sean niveles cada vez más difíciles hasta convertirse en imposibles, por lo que el juego harta rápido y terminas sacándolo sin querer saber más de el.

The game is pretty hard, but the controls are decent. The pixel style is sometimes a bit off (you really see it when certain sprites are scaled and the character sprite has larger pixels than the power ups, buts thats really nit-picking here). Soundtrack is also fitting. 

It feels like someone put a lot of work and heart into this project. It is not as polished as Super Meatboy, but it's still great fun.

While this game is quite difficult to get used to I think it has a great deal of potential. There are a few small things I would change to make this game a little less punishing.

1. Let the arrow keys move the character a bit while falling. I'm aware that gravity changes allow you to change your course, however it'd be nice to be able to rely on falling to do things and to counteract the intertia you invariably have when coming off a ledge.

2. Give a bit of leeway on the outside of the map for falling or whatever. It'd be nioce if you could extend the buffer to about 3 or 4 tiles so that going off the map isn't insta-death. If something is insta-death then use spikes instead.

3. A windowed mode?

However, it is a challenging game and I can see the fun in it.
